title: Feasibility and Safety Study of Novel Mechanical Thromboprophylaxis Device in Critically Ill Pediatric Patients
official: Feasibility and Safety Study of Novel Mechanical Thromboprophylaxis Device in Critically Ill Pediatric Patients
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the use, feasibility, and safety of the Recovery Force Health (RFH) Movement and Compression (MAC) System for mechanical prevention of hospital acquired blood clots, in critically ill children ages 3 to 17 years admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. In adolescents ages 12 to 17 years of age, does the RFH MAC System achieve an average compliance rate at least 25% higher than the standard sequential compression device (SCD)?
2. Is the RFH MAC System feasible and safe to use in children ages 3 to 11 years?
3. How do clinical staff rate the usability, efficiency, and overall satisfaction of the RFH MAC System with the standard sequential compression device?

Researchers will compare the RFH MAC System with the Kendall SCD 700 Series in adolescent ages 12 to 17 years to determine whether the RFH MAC System improves compliance with mechanical blood clot prevention. Children ages 3 to 11 will receive the RFH MAC System only, with no comparison group.

Participants will:

1. Use one of the devices during their PICU stay if they are ages 12 to 17 years or use the RFH MAC System if they are ages 3 to 11 years.
2. Have their calf circumference collected to help inform device sizing.

Clinical staff will complete questionnaires after the intervention about device usability, feasibility, and overall satisfaction.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Patients aged 12 - \<18 years of age at the time of PICU admission (Adolescent Cohort Only)
2. Patients ages 3 - \<12 years at the time of PICU admission (Children Cohort Only)
3. Patients with a minimum calf circumference of 20.30 centimeters.
4. Patients admitted to the PICU at Cook Children's.
5. Patients that meet any of the following venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk criteria (Adolescent Cohort Only) 5a.Patients with a moderate VTE Risk score (4-6) per institutional VTE risk score at the time of PICU admission, OR 5b. Patients with a high VTE risk score (\>6) per the institutional VTE risk score and with any of the following pharmacological prophylaxis contraindications at the time of PICU admission: 5b1. Inability to maintain platelet count \> 50 x 109/L 5b2. Inability to correct coagulopathy 5b3. Post-operative bleeding concerns 5b4. Active hemorrhage 5b5. Epidural/spinal catheter in place (or in prior 12-24 hours) 5b6. Extra ventricular drain in place (or in prior 24 hours) 5b7. Intracranial pressure monitors in place (or in prior 24 hours) 5b8. Craniotomy within 2 weeks 5b9. Severe trauma to head or spinal cord with hemorrhage within 2-4 weeks 5b10. Intracranial lesions/neoplasms 5b11. Hypertensive urgency/emergency 5b12. Congenital bleeding disorder 5b13. Aspirin (unless needs for disease management) 5b14. High dose non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs 5b15. Heparin induced thrombocytopenia 5b16. Allergy to pork or religious objection
6. Patients currently with CVC or PICC in place in lower extremity(ies) (Children Cohort Only)

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Patients that do not meet the age criteria at the time of PICU admission.
2. Adolescent patients (12-\<18 years) without VTE risk screening assessment
3. Adolescent patient (12-\<18 years) with VTE risk screening assessment completed beyond 24 hours of admission.
4. Adolescent patients (12-\<18 years) with low VTE risk (0-3)
5. Female patients that are pregnant at the time of admission.
6. Patients with superficial vein thrombosis present at admission.
7. Patients currently on anticoagulation therapy.
8. Patients with severe pain, acute fractures of extremity, burns, and skin breakdown/dermatitis.
9. Patient who has undergone an amputation or limb loss.
10. Patients with peripheral intravenous (IV) catheter in lower extremity.
11. Any local condition in which the sleeves/straps may interfere. (e.g., open wounds, ulcers, grafts, flaps, cellulitis, dermatitis, large dressings, casts, external fixators, or other devices that prevent safe fitting).
12. Ischemic vascular disease (e.g., known peripheral arterial disease, limb ischemia, and ischemic ulcers), where compression could further compromise arterial blood flow.
13. Significant Edema of the legs (Grade 3 or 4)
14. Extreme deformity of the leg. (e.g., contractures, congenital or post traumatic deformity) that prevents proper fitting or results in uneven pressure.
15. Suspected or confirmed deep or superficial venous thrombosis.
16. Presence of unexplained calf pain.
17. Medical conditions where increased venous and lymphatic return are undesirable. (e.g., heart failure, pulmonary hypertension), as assessed by the principal investigator (PI)/PICU attending/Sub-Investigators (Sub-Is).
18. Any condition in which the PI feels would put the patient at additional risk by participating in this study.
19. Amputated lower extremity (both legs).
